design_goal.primary: Design a foldable 50-aa binder that forms a high-confidence interface localized to fixed ASYN residues 99-140.
design_goal.formal_success_definition: A candidate preserves the exact 140-aa ASYN target, remains exactly 50 canonical residues and developable, and forms a clash-controlled holo interface whose ASYN contacts are enriched in residues 99-140.

positive_signals: At least one direct binder-ASYN residue pair lies inside ASYN residues 99-140.
Most ASYN-side interface residue pairs fall inside residues 99-140.
The binder avoids excessive hydrophobicity, cysteine burden, and long homopolymers.
The binder has acceptable confidence inside the holo complex.
The holo complex has usable ipTM/PAE-derived confidence and a contact-rich binder-ASYN interface.
failure_signals: Any ASYN residue changes or the ASYN chain length changes.
No direct binder contact reaches ASYN residues 99-140.
Required holo complex structure evidence is missing.
The apparent interface is dominated by ASYN residues outside 99-140.
The binder is not exactly 50 canonical amino acids.
The interface contains excessive steric clashes.

information_gaps: ESMFold confidence, pTM, PAE, and contact geometry are structural proxies requiring experimental binding validation.
The ASYN C terminus is intrinsically disordered; low hotspot pLDDT is not a failure criterion.
No negative target or off-target state is included in this first case version.
Experimental binding, specificity, solubility, and aggregation assays are required.
provisional_assumptions: The biological hotspot is ASYN residues 99-140, mapped to zero-based [98,140).
Candidates compared within one run use the same sealed provider mode, seeds, and sampling protocol.
The starting binder is the fixed 50-residue Bagel state-0 sequence. The five search nodes form a resizable contiguous partition over all 50 binder positions.
